purpose: Track external Hebrew affect/pragmatics resources without treating them as reader-effect ground truth.

sources.name: Hebrew VAD Lexicon
sources.annotation_origin: English VAD-derived resource adapted to Hebrew with manual correction/enrichment
sources.use: lexical affect reference and feature substrate
risk_notes: Scores inherit mapping/aggregation assumptions from English source words.
Do not treat lexical VAD as sentence pragmatics or recipient effect.

sources.name: VAD Knesset Corpus — manually annotated subset
risk_notes: Parliamentary domain may not transfer to colloquial Israeli Hebrew.
VAD is not a direct recipient-effect annotation.

sources.name: hebnoRms / E-Millim-derived affect norms
sources.license: GPL-3.0 for package; verify underlying resource terms before redistribution
sources.size: 22K and up to ~1.4M Hebrew token forms
sources.annotation_origin: E-Millim affective norms expanded with distributional methods
sources.use: broad lexical coverage and morphology-sensitive affect reference
risk_notes: Expansion is heuristic/model-based beyond the original human norms.
Use as substrate, not adjudication truth for pragmatics.

sources.name: HebEMO / HeBERT emotion corpus
sources.annotation_origin: human annotation of Hebrew UGC subset
risk_notes: Emotion expressed/perceived in text is not the same construct as emotion induced in the reader.
Freeze a subset before any Hebrew-specific Neta update.

sources.name: IronySet
risk_notes: News-register Hebrew differs from colloquial dialogue.
Do not infer recipient emotion directly from irony labels.

construction_gap.missing_resource: Native-Hebrew sentence/dialogue corpus with direct recipient self-report of induced interpersonal effect
construction_gap.anti_build_rule: Do not recreate lexical sentiment/emotion resources already available; build only the missing reader-effect layer.
